content:
Never let it be said that President Donald Trump doesn’t have his priorities. He just hates being questioned about them.

Case in point: The unhinged response he gave on Monday to NBC White House correspondent Yamiche Alcindor.

It all started after Alcindor asked the president if his obsession with construction projects like the White House Ballroom was taking focus away from the country’s current aviation infrastructure debacle.

“Mr. President, what do you say to critics who say you were too focused on D.C. construction projects while our airline systems were crumbling, given the fact that Republicans have been in control?” she asked.

Trump’s first instinct was to turn the pointed question into praise for the work on the White House, sprinkled with a touch of racism towards Alcindor, who is Black.

“Well, if you take a look at the White House, it’s flawless. Listen to me — I know you don’t see dirt — but if you’d take a look at the White House, you’d never notice broken windows, obviously, from where you come. I don’t know. But we had 18 broken windows.”

Trump claimed the exterior plaster “was falling off the wall,” and “was an embarrassment,” before rambling further about the construction, adding that “the helipad has gotten great reviews.”

Alcindor then attempted to ask about Friday’s air traffic shutdown, which Trump avoided commenting on for much of the weekend.

“What responsibility do you take?” Alcindor asked regarding the air traffic shutdown, which Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy blamed on an aging system.

“Could you have given more money—” she asked before Trump interrupted her with an insult.

“Oh, you’re so pathetic!” Trump said. “Listen, I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape. And it takes me 10 minutes a day — very little time. Ten minutes a day. I have people — I don’t do it. You don’t see me on a scaffold.”

Alcindor tried again.

“But why hasn’t there been more funding to our crumbling airline system, given—” she asked before Trump cut her off again.

“This doesn’t cost money,” Trump said. “This is peanuts. And I pay for it. This doesn’t cost money; this is peanuts, this is called talent. Talent. You don’t have talent. You don’t know what a broken column is.”

Trump may not have liked the question, but Alcindor got a lot of support from fellow reporters and politicians.

This isn’t the first time Trump has insulted Alcindor to her face.

Back in September 2025, after Trump threatened to sic the “Department of War” on Chicago in a social media post, Alcindor asked if he was trying to “go to war” with the Windy City.

“When you say that, darling, that’s fake news,” he snapped, and got even angrier when she tried to follow up.

“Listen. Be quiet. Listen,” he grumbled. “You don’t listen. You never listen. That’s why you’re second-rate.”

In June, 2020, Trump got testy when trying to praise a slight improvement in overall unemployment numbers when Alcindor noted that unemployment for African American and Asian citizens had actually increased.

“You are something else,” he griped.
